outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Tuten turned 28 carries and three targets into 150 scrimmage yards and one TD. The speedster is a viable RB3/flex for Week 3, though expectations should be tempered against a New England defense that's off to an elite start, having allowed just 16 points through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 80 scrimmage yards and takes a two-game touchdown streak into Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals. Tuten is locked in atop the running back depth chart in one of the league's best offenses, which makes him a reliable fantasy RB2, even with Chris Rodriguez, LeQuint Allen, and Ameer Abdullah siphoning touches here and there. Cincinnati has been better than average against the run, but the Bengals have allowed a league-high 141 receiving yards to RBs, so Tuten is likely to make some plays as a pass-catcher even if running room is hard to come by.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bhayshul Tuten has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in three of the first four games of his second season with the Jaguars. The 2025 fourth-round pick has thrived in the lead role, establishing himself as an every-week fantasy RB2. He'll face an Eagles defense in Week 5 that's allowing 106 rushing yards per game to RBs and just surrendered a pair of late rushing scores to the Rams' Kyren Williams in a Week 4 loss. Tuten and the Jaguars will have a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff Sunday in Week 5 when they face the Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bhayshul Tuten remains Jacksonville's starting RB heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans. He has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in four of five games while occupying that role and has two rushing TDs this season. Houston has been among the league's stingiest defenses against RBs, limiting the position to 89 scrimmage yards per game and allowing only three TDs on 103 carries. Tuten's prominent role in an above-average offense keeps him in the fantasy RB2 range despite the tricky Week 6 matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trevor Lawrence threw for a season-high 331 yards against the Eagles as the Jaguars improved to 4-1 with a Week 5 win. He brings a 10:3 TD:INT into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans, which will be the Jaguars' second consecutive game in London. Houston has surprisingly been one of the league's most generous pass defenses, allowing QBs to throw for 256 yards per game, though the Texans have allowed only six TDs through the air. Lawrence produced just 380 passing yards with a 1:2 TD:INT in two meetings with the AFC South rival Texans in 2025, but since Houston's defense has taken a step back this season, Lawrence can continue to be deployed as a starting fantasy QB for Week 6.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.7: Jawhar Jordan would be on the radar in deeper fantasy formats for Week 7 against the Giants if fellow Texans RB David Montgomery (groin) missed a second consecutive game. Jordan excelled in a change-of-pace role behind Woody Marks in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville, turning six carries and one target into 50 scrimmage yards, with half of that yardage coming on a 25-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. If Montgomery returns, Jordan would be hard-pressed to earn much playing time as the third-string RB option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of those.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of them.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but led the Texans to just six points in the absence of top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) during Week 2's loss to the Bengals. If Houston remains without Collins in Week 3 against the Colts, Stroud will likely lean heavily on TE Dalton Schultz once more against a Colts defense that allowed 41 points to the Ravens and then 33 to the Chiefs. Considering the Colts have surrendered the most points and yards in the NFL, Stroud is worth a look in superflex or multi-QB lineups, but he will likely remain ranked outside the starting range in single-QB formats, at least until Collins returns.
outlooksByWeek.4: C.J. Stroud has missed top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) over Houston's past two games, failing to throw a touchdown pass in Week 2 and producing just 167 passing yards in Week 3. The Texans fell to 0-3 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. On the bright side, the Texans rebounded from an 0-3 start last season to finish 12-5, and Collins has a realistic chance to return versus Dallas. If Stroud gets his top target back, the slumping QB would have a nice opportunity to get on track as a strong superflex or second fantasy QB against a weak Cowboys secondary that has allowed a 7:0 TD:INT through three games in 2026 after giving up the most QB production in the league last season. Should Collins sit again, Stroud would be a risky choice in all formats despite the favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: C.J. Stroud has some streaming appeal in single-QB formats for Week 5, when the Texans travel to Tennessee for a battle between 0-4 AFC South squads. He has thrown for at least 347 yards in two of Houston's four losses and has a 5:0 TD:INT. The Titans have been respectable against the pass, with only four touchdowns allowed through the air this season, but other teams were able to build leads and run effectively on Tennessee. The Texans are unlikely to find as much success on the ground, considering RBs David Montgomery and Woody Marks have combined to average 2.9 yards per carry this season. Stroud has been asked to throw the ball 38 times per game, and he's likely to remain busy in Week 5. The Texans got top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence in Week 4, and Collins contributed immediately in his return by catching both of Stroud's touchdown passes in a 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
outlooksByWeek.6: C.J. Stroud could have a key new target for Houston's pivotal Week 6 clash with the AFC South-leading Jaguars in London. The Texans are just 1-4 and have already fallen three games behind Jacksonville in the standings, but Stroud is quietly averaging a career-high 280 passing yards per game to go with a 6:0 TD:INT. Jacksonville gives up the fewest rushing yards and second-most passing yards per game, so Stroud will likely be asked to carry Houston's offense again in Week 6, making him a viable starting QB in fantasy. The Texans notched their first win of the season in Week 5 over the Titans and promptly traded for disgruntled Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison, who hasn't lived up to the hype as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft but excelled at Ohio State while catching passes from Stroud in 2022. Harrison likely won't be fully up to speed, but he could still provide an upgrade over Houston's current wideouts behind Nico Collins.
outlooksByWeek.7: C.J. Stroud is averaging a career-high 286 passing yards per game and has posted a 9:1 TD:INT heading into Houston's Week 7 home game against the Giants. He threw a season-high three touchdown passes in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville while topping 300 yards for the third time in six starts. The Giants have surrendered 12 passing TDs, which is sixth-most in the NFL, and their three rushing scores allowed to QBs are tied for the most in the league, though they have also notched six interceptions. Stroud has consistently been asked to put the Texans' offense on his back due to the team's weak running game, and he has mostly been up to the challenge, so he remains a fringe fantasy starter for Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.
